title: Accept & Proceed’s new system for Vans is a lesson in how to inject clarity into an iconic brand

paragraphs.text: The visual and conceptual overhaul of the shoemaker speaks to the brand’s place in culture and its role as a conduit for expression.
paragraphs.translation: 這次對鞋履製造商的視覺與概念大改造，展現了該品牌在文化中的地位，以及其作為表達媒介的角色。

paragraphs.text: There aren’t many shoes more iconic than Vans, whether it’s their silhouette, chequered patterns or place in pop culture; you know a pair of Vans when you see them. From a branding perspective, however, it’s not quite as singular. Whilst its logo hasn’t changed much since, if at all, since it was founded in 1966, it’s had a number of owners and eras across the decades that followed, leaving a somewhat fragmented brand in its place. This was the problem faced by London-based design studio Accept & Proceed, who have completely rewired that brand’s visual and conceptual foundation, culminating in a new brand system, standards and product branding guidelines.
paragraphs.translation: 很少有鞋子比 Vans 更具代表性，無論是其輪廓、棋盤格紋，還是在流行文化中的地位；你只要看到一雙 Vans 就能認出來。然而，從品牌經營的角度來看，它並非如此單一。雖然其標誌自 1966 年創立以來幾乎沒有改變，但在隨後的數十年間，它歷經了多位擁有者和不同的時代，留下了一個有些支離破碎的品牌。這是總部位於倫敦的設計工作室 Accept & Proceed 所面臨的問題，他們完全重塑了該品牌的視覺與概念基礎，最終形成了一套新的品牌系統、標準和產品品牌指南。

paragraphs.text: This reset and new standardisation – providing the shoemaker with greater clarity and consistency across the entire brand – is conceptually-led, guided by the north star: ‘Our Canvas. Your Way.’ Speaking to Vans’ history and how its products have been adopted, customised and used as a medium for expression, the concept centres the brand’s relationship with communities at the heart of its output. “Rather than replacing the brand’s existing assets, we created a simple two-layer framework that gave them a clearer role to play,” Accept & Proceed’s creative director, Stephen Heath, says, defining what remains fixed within the system and what can flex. “It stays true to the origins of Vans,” Stephen adds, “while giving future teams the freedom to express it in ways that feel relevant to new audiences.” In essence, the studio have created a system that encourages participation over stringent control.
paragraphs.translation: 這次重置與新的標準化——為這家鞋商在整個品牌中提供了更高的清晰度與一致性——是以概念為導向的，並由指引方針「我們的畫布，你的方式」所領導。這項概念呼應了 Vans 的歷史，以及其產品如何被大眾採用、客製化並作為表達媒介，將品牌與社群的關係置於其產出的核心。Accept & Proceed 的創意總監 Stephen Heath 表示：「我們並非更換品牌現有的資產，而是建立了一個簡單的兩層架構，賦予它們更明確的角色」，這定義了系統中哪些部分保持不變，哪些部分可以靈活調整。Stephen 補充道：「它忠於 Vans 的起源，同時賦予未來團隊自由，以符合新受眾的方式來表達它。」本質上，該工作室創造了一個鼓勵參與而非嚴格控制的系統。

paragraphs.text: Accept & Proceed began the project by stripping the brand back to its very basics. “We asked what genuinely made Vans recognisably Vans,” Stephen says. “Once we understood those core ingredients, it became clear that the role of the system wasn’t to create more rules. We then undertook a comprehensive audit of how the brand was applied across the entire product portfolio,” finding the inconsistency and opportunities throughout Vans’ output. “The resulting product branding standards helped define the constants,” Stephen says, “while giving teams the confidence and flexibility to apply the brand more coherently.”
paragraphs.translation: Accept & Proceed 在開始此專案時，將品牌簡化至最基本的要素。Stephen 說：「我們詢問什麼是真正讓 Vans 具備辨識度的特質。一旦我們理解了這些核心成分，就很清楚系統的作用並非建立更多規則。接著我們對品牌在整個產品組合中的應用進行了全面審計」，發現了 Vans 產出中的不一致之處與機會。Stephen 說：「最終的產品品牌標準有助於定義恆定量，同時讓團隊有信心且靈活地更連貫地應用品牌。」

paragraphs.text: This ethos is only expanded through the brand’s approach to typography. “We introduced Pitch Mono as a supporting voice, adding a more functional, expressive layer,” Stephen explains, with the monospace typeface complementing Vans’ existing Fann Doren family. “We placed greater emphasis on its condensed styles to improve consistency and confidence in application,” he adds. They deliberately didn’t tinker with the typography too much, and instead opted to clarify what they already have.
paragraphs.translation: 這種理念在品牌的字體處理方式中得到了進一步擴展。Stephen 解釋道：「我們引入了 Pitch Mono 作為輔助聲音，增加了一個更具功能性且富表現力的層次」，這款等寬字體與 Vans 現有的 Fann Doren 系列相輔相成。他補充說：「我們更加強調其窄體風格，以提高應用中的一致性與信心。」他們刻意沒有對字體進行太多修改，而是選擇釐清現有的資產。

paragraphs.text: “Like any project of this scale, there were many different stakeholder perspectives to balance,” Stephen says, “but the bigger challenge was cultural.” After all, sports and subcultures like skateboarding are fiercely independent and, as Stephen suggests, “sceptical of anything that feels manufactured”. So Accept & Proceed needed to strike a balance between creating a brand system that respected what came before and allowing the brand to grow beyond it. “The breakthrough came when we stopped thinking about Vans as a skate brand,” he says, “and started thinking about it as a brand built around a spirit of creative possibility,” ends Stephen. “That gave us a framework that could honour its roots, while creating space for its new audiences, sports and forms of expression.”
paragraphs.translation: Stephen 說：「像任何這種規模的專案一樣，有許多不同利害關係人的觀點需要平衡，但更大的挑戰在於文化。」畢竟，像滑板這樣的運動和次文化是極度獨立的，正如 Stephen 所暗示的，它們「對任何感覺像是刻意製造的東西都持懷疑態度」。因此，Accept & Proceed 需要在建立一個尊重過去的品牌系統，與允許品牌超越過去成長之間取得平衡。他最後說道：「當我們不再把 Vans 視為一個滑板品牌，而開始把它視為一個圍繞創意可能性精神建立的品牌時，突破就出現了。這給了我們一個框架，既能傳承其根源，又能為新的受眾、運動和表達形式創造空間。」
